title: fix: update EC2 monitor setup and failure reporting
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Documents the monitoring-agents EC2 migration and existing Discord bot launchers/systemd units.
- Hides community models below 50% success across at least 10 requests in four hours only after a fresh provider-failing probe; passing, client/auth/payment, or inconclusive probes veto hiding.
- Treats terminal usage errors as failed requests, distinct from informational billing flags; checks provider versus shared gateway causes before attributing failures.
- Makes the committed prompt authoritative over old memories and documents removing frozen prompt overrides while preserving counters and cooldowns.
- Updates from main and corrects the live host inventory to 200 GB disk / 30 GB swap. Gateway validation and billing are unchanged.

Validation: reviewed the complete diff; Biome, JavaScript syntax, shell syntax, and PR whitespace checks passed. EC2 activation and prompt verification will run after merge. No credential changes or Discord bot restarts are included.

gist.headline: The garden checks twice
gist.blurb: The community-model gardener got stricter about evidence before putting a wilting model behind the hedge. Fresh provider checks now separate real outages from billing notes, bad requests, and gateway weather.
gist.summary: Community monitoring now hides a model only when it falls below 50% success across at least 10 requests in four hours and a fresh probe confirms a provider-side failure, while passing, client/auth/payment, and inconclusive probes veto hiding.
gist.impact: Users get a more reliable community-model list: genuine provider failures are filtered sooner, while models are kept visible when errors come from client requests, authentication, payment, or uncertain gateway causes.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy model-health garden where Polli acts as a careful gardener, checking a drooping code-flower with a fresh diagnostic probe before moving it behind a small hedge. A helpful CRT monitor robot displays distinct provider, gateway, billing, and client-error signals, making it clear that only confirmed provider failures trigger the garden's protective filtering.
